subject: Integration qualification: CureLytics SDK & streaming/function-calls fit
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@curelytics.com>, Renee O'Connell <renee@curelytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Integration qualification: CureLytics SDK & streaming/function-calls fit

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the candid chat. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on product fit and technical constraints.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Latency-sensitive inference for clinical triage (95th pct target ~250ms for short prompts)
- Desire to run reranker on embeddings + streaming summaries into your clinical UI
- Need for deterministic structured outputs for downstream ingestion (JSON schema validated)
- Tight data residency and audit requirements for PHI workflows (on-prem or VPC options considered)

What we think fits well from Redwood:
- Streaming token-by-token responses with early-commit hooks so your UI can render partial summaries while reranker runs in parallel
- Function-calling / structured output support to return typed JSON for extraction into your EHR pipeline
- Embeddings + rerank pipeline: we recommend embedding on a quantized open model and running a lightweight reranker on a dedicated instance to meet latency targets

Technical open items we need to confirm:
1) Typical prompt + context size (tokens) you expect for triage and summarization flows
2) SLA/throughput targets (reqs per second) for peak hours
3) Whether PHI will always be in-scope for these calls (affects Private deployment requirement and KMS needs)

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline):
- Action (Jonas): share SDK compatibility matrix + short PoC plan (attached) — by 2027-03-16
- Action (CureLytics): share sample prompt/response examples and your JSON schema for structured outputs — by 2027-03-18
- Action (Ben & Neha): scope a small dedicated pilot (2 GPUs) and estimate costs/latency — internal by 2027-03-19

Attachments: redwood-sdk-compatibility-matrix.pdf (SDKs, language bindings, streaming examples), curelytics-integration-checklist.xlsx (minimal PoC checklist).

If that looks good I'll set up a follow-up with our solutions engineer to draft a PoC and data/security checklist.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Samir Patel <samir@curelytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Renee O'Connell <renee@curelytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration qualification: CureLytics SDK & streaming/function-calls fit

Jonas — thanks for the write-up and for the attachments. Quick answers and a couple clarifying items below.

Short answers:
- Typical context window: 600–1,200 tokens for triage prompts; summaries often <300 tokens.
- Peak throughput: expect up to 40 reqs/s during morning batch windows; typical sustained 5–8 reqs/s.
- PHI: yes, triage data can include sensitive patient notes; on-prem/VPC with HSM is our preferred route for production.

Clarifying questions:
1) For function-calling: can Redwood enforce schema validation server-side and return typed errors so we can fail-fast on malformed data?
2) For reranker: can we run the embedding step in hosted (to use faster GPUs) and the reranker on Dedicated instances for deterministic latency? Any data egress concerns?

We'll pull together the JSON schema for the structured outputs and share a few example prompts by end of day Friday. Would like Ben on the next call to review pilot sizing.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Systems | CureLytics
samir@curelytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@curelytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration qualification: CureLytics SDK & streaming/function-calls fit

Appreciate the fast responses Samir. To Samir's questions:
- Schema validation: yes — Redwood can validate function-call payloads against a provided JSON schema and return a structured error object (error_code, field_errors array) before invoking model execution. That validation step can be enforced at the control plane for Hosted and at the Private control plane for on-prem.
- Hybrid embeddings/reranker: we support split pipelines. Embeddings can run on Hosted for cost/perf and then results (vector IDs or embeddings) can be forwarded to Dedicated reranker instances. Egress is configurable: if vectors are considered PHI you can keep everything in Private; otherwise we can set up strict network controls (VPC peering + IP allowlists).

Pilot suggestion (2-week PoC):
- Week 1: Integration & streaming validation (token streaming, early-commit hooks, SDK examples). Run 1000 sample prompts to confirm 95th pct latency for <300-token responses.
- Week 2: Embeddings + rerank pipeline with sample dataset, validate top-K recall and end-to-end latency.

I'll scope GPU sizing and a rough cost estimate and post by Friday. Neha will own security checklist and will follow up with required logs/audit samples.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Renee O'Connell <renee@curelytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@curelytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration qualification: CureLytics SDK & streaming/function-calls fit

Thanks team — this is helpful and actionable. Confirming next steps from our side:
- We will send the structured-output JSON schema and 25 representative prompt/response pairs by 2027-03-18.
- We can provision a staging dataset for reranking (approx 10k items) for your PoC.
- Security: PHI is sensitive for us; please include a sample Private deployment checklist (KMS, audit logs, retention policy) in your security notes.

We'd like to schedule the solutions-engineer PoC kickoff for the week of 2027-03-22. Can you propose 2 slots? Prefer mornings PST.

Best,
Renee O'Connell
Head of Product Operations | CureLytics
renee@curelytics.com
